name: @projexlight/sdk-api-keys
summary: Long-lived programmatic credentials for ProjexCloud: issue per-tenant API keys bound to a service-persona with a scope list, rotate with a grace window, revoke instantly. Hashes only — we never store the secret bytes; the customer sees the secret exactly once at issue time. Hot-path verifier is sub-ms because it reads from the projection layer + a Redis cache.

endpoints.description: Issue a new key for (tenant, service_persona). Returns the secret EXACTLY ONCE; only the hash is stored.
List active keys for the calling tenant (name, prefix, scopes, last_used_at, expires_at). Secrets are never returned.
Immediate revoke. Hot-path cache invalidated within the route-cache TTL.
Rotate: mint a new secret under the same key_id; old secret valid for 10-min grace window for zero-downtime swap.

events.name: api-keys.issued.v1
events.description: New key minted; carries key_id + prefix (never the secret).

events.name: api-keys.rotated.v1
events.description: Key rotated; old + new key_version refs.

events.name: api-keys.revoked.v1
events.description: Key revoked instantly. Cache invalidation broadcast.

events.name: api-keys.verification.failed.v1
events.description: Failed-auth observability (signal: brute-force attempt? stale config?). Rate-limited per key prefix.

models.description: Per-key row: key_id, tenant_id, service_persona_id, prefix, hash_envelope (SHA-256 of secret, vault-wrapped), scopes, expires_at, status.

hooks.name: issueKey
hooks.description: Service entry. Secret returned only here; the call should immediately hand the secret to the customer + clear from memory.

hooks.name: verifyKey
hooks.description: Hot-path verifier. Sub-ms when the cache is warm; falls back to projection + DB on miss. Used by the gateway preHandler when Authorization is `Bearer apikey_*`.

hooks.name: rotateKey
hooks.description: Mint a new secret under the same key_id; old secret stays valid for the grace window (default 10 min).

hooks.name: revokeKey
hooks.description: Instant revoke + cache invalidation broadcast on Redis. No grace window.

scenarios.title: Customer issues an API key for their CI pipeline
scenarios.when_to_use: Tenant admin needs a long-lived M2M credential for GitHub Actions / GitLab CI / Jenkins.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns the secret exactly once + a non-secret prefix. Emits api-keys.issued.v1. Subsequent listKeys() shows the prefix + scopes + expiry but NEVER the secret.

scenarios.title: Gateway hot-path verifies the key on every request
scenarios.when_to_use: preHandler that runs on every Authorization: Bearer apikey_* request. Sub-ms is non-negotiable here.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns the six-layer claim set matching the service-persona, or null. Cache miss writes warm-entry on success.

scenarios.title: Rotate quarterly with zero-downtime config swap
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer rotates their CI secret per policy. They want a window to update the secret in their CI without dropping builds.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns the new secret. Both old + new accepted by verifyKey for the grace window. After grace expires, old is silently rejected. Emits api-keys.rotated.v1.

scenarios.title: Revoke instantly after a suspected leak
scenarios.when_to_use: Security incident — customer believes their CI runner was compromised. Need immediate revocation, no grace window.
scenarios.example_code:
import { revokeKey } from '@projexlight/sdk-api-keys';
await revokeKey({ key_id, reason: 'suspected leak in CI logs' });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Key flipped to revoked. Redis pub/sub broadcasts the invalidation across every gateway replica within the route-cache TTL. Emits api-keys.revoked.v1 with the reason for the audit trail.

scenarios.title: Reissue a key with narrower scopes (least-privilege follow-up)
scenarios.when_to_use: Audit finds the old key had broader scopes than the workload actually needs; reissue narrower; revoke the old one.
scenarios.expected_outcome: New key in service with minimum-privilege scopes. Audit chain shows the deprecation flow. Compliance report (SOC2 CC6.6) shows the reduction in privilege over time.

compliance_posture.notes: Secrets never persisted in plaintext — only SHA-256 hash, vault-wrapped. Customer-visible secret returned exactly once at issue time. Rotation grace window keeps M2M integrations functional; revoke is immediate (no grace). Audit chain attestation supports SOC2 CC6.6 logical-access review evidence.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per key issued (rotate counts as a new issue for billing)
per verify call (most are cache hits; cache misses billed at a higher rate)
